newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks rise on resumed blue-chip interest.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks rise on resumed blue-chip interest.

text.p: Jordanian shares rose on Tuesday in healthy trade boosted by revived interest in blue-chip shares, brokers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.29 percent to 164.16 points in trade worth 1.6 million dinars ($2.3 million).
"There's more institutional demand, both local and foreign," said analyst Mohammad Abdallah of Pearl Consulting.
Arab Bank, which has dominated trade in the bourse for the last week, recouped most of Monday's losses, gaining 1.5 dinars to close at 279.5 dinars after turnover worth nearly 400,000 dinars.
Brokers attribute its recent popularity to forecasts of strong 1997 profits, expectations of a bonus share offering, and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.
"It will probably stay around the 280 dinar level until the foreign (ownership) ceilings are removed," Abdallah said. "After that it could reach above 300."
But other blue-chips, which have taken a back seat for the last few days while traders concentrated on Arab Bank, returned to the spotlight on Tuesday.

The Housing Bank and Jordan Cement Factories, which have been targeted by international investors, both traded heavily. Housing Bank gained 0.01 dinars to 4.91 and the cement factory shares were unchanged after turnover of 200,000 dinars.
Gainers outnumbered decliners for the first time this week, with 18 climbing and 10 falling. Another 10 shares traded but closed unchanged.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.08 percent to 80.55 points, 3.40 percent down from the start of the year. $1 = 0.709 dinars
